forces.title: AI adoption and digital transformation in real estate services
forces.description: The adoption of Artificial Intelligence in India's corporate real estate sector increased from less than 5% in 2023 to 91% in 2025, transforming planning, construction, asset management, and property transactions. Real estate services companies are advised to leverage AI for proprietary workflows and data, streamlining manual processes like billing. This shift creates a structural need for PropTech solutions and expertise, redefining operational efficiencies and competitive differentiation for service providers.

forces.title: Strong growth in commercial office leasing driving service demand
forces.description: India's commercial office leasing activity remains robust, with foreign companies leasing a record 9.10 million sq. ft. in Q1 2026 and gross office leasing reaching an all-time high of 24.60 million sq. ft. in Q2 2026. This sustained demand, particularly from Global Capability Centres (GCCs), multinational corporations, and flexible workspace operators, directly fuels the need for property brokers, transaction advisors, and property managers in the commercial real estate services segment.

forces.title: Favorable regulatory environment enhancing REIT market and investments
forces.description: SEBI's REIT (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, aim to strengthen the regulatory framework, improve governance, transparency, and investor protection, and broaden investment opportunities in India's REIT market. This policy support fosters institutional investor confidence and encourages greater capital inflows into real estate. Such an environment creates increased demand for specialized real estate services, including transaction advisory for REIT listings and acquisitions, and professional property management for REIT-owned assets, ensuring market integrity and growth.

forces.title: Emergence of flexible workspaces boosting property management demand
forces.description: Flexible workspace operators are significantly impacting the office market, accounting for 25.9% of total office leasing in Q1 2026 and renting a record 2.24 lakh seats in 2024. This trend signals a structural shift towards managed and hybrid office solutions, driven by corporate demand. This creates robust opportunities for specialized property management services, facility management, and brokerage for co-working spaces, particularly in major cities, establishing a distinct and growing sub-segment within real estate services.

forces.title: Increased institutional investments fueling real estate transaction activity
forces.description: Institutional investments in India's real estate sector reached a record Rs. 94,120 crore (US$ 10.40 billion) in 2025, with strong momentum continuing into Q1 2026, reaching Rs. 1.06 lakh crore (US$ 1.20 billion). Domestic investors contributed 57% of inflows, primarily directed towards office assets and mixed-use developments. This surge in capital deployment, including M&A transactions, directly translates into higher demand for transaction advisors, property brokers, and appraisal services as investors seek to acquire, manage, and divest real estate assets.

forces.title: Overall real estate market growth supports demand for services
forces.description: India's real estate market is projected to expand significantly from US$ 650 billion in 2025 to US$ 5.80 trillion by 2047, driven by rapid urbanization and strong economic growth. This foundational expansion across residential, commercial, retail, industrial, and logistics segments inherently generates increased demand for all types of real estate services, including brokerage, property management, and appraisal, as market activity scales proportionally with sector development and transactions.

forces.title: Growth in data center real estate creating specialized service opportunities
forces.description: India's data center capacity is rapidly expanding, with an estimated construction-related opportunity of USD30 billion by FY30 and USD90 billion by FY35. This growth is driven by increasing digital needs, AI workloads, and hyperscaler investments. This creates significant demand for specialized real estate services such as project management consultants, design consultants, and commissioning services for data center facilities, representing a high-value segment for IN110501 due to its technical complexity and scale.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: AI-native data center design necessitating advanced real estate services
forces.description: The transition to AI-native data centers demands a full-scale redesign of infrastructure, requiring higher structural load ratings, significantly higher power densities (50-60 kW/rack vs. 8-12 kW/rack), and advanced liquid cooling. This fundamental shift from traditional specifications necessitates specialized real estate services expertise in design, engineering, and project management, pushing service providers to adapt to more technologically advanced and complex projects in this segment, creating a new standard for service delivery.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: Monetary policy easing improving housing affordability and demand
forces.description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reduced the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.25% in December 2025, improving home loan affordability for consumers. This policy easing supports sustained growth in the residential real estate sector by boosting buyer confidence and demand. A healthy residential market directly translates to increased activity for property brokers and transaction advisors dealing with home sales and rentals, particularly as residential launches and sales remain robust.

forces.title: Government initiatives streamlining land records and approvals
forces.description: Government programs like the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme and streamlining of approval and arbitration processes, ongoing since 2016, enhance transparency and accelerate project approvals. The geo-referencing of land parcels and integration of sub-registrar offices reduce title disputes. This supportive policy environment simplifies property transactions, benefiting property brokers, transaction advisors, and real estate data platforms by reducing friction, improving reliability, and speeding up deal closures, thereby boosting efficiency.

forces.title: Localisation opportunity in data center construction value chain
forces.description: India's data center supplier ecosystem is at an inflection point, with a significant opportunity for domestic players to localize manufacturing and deploy AI-native data center capabilities across the value chain. This presents an upside for Indian real estate service providers specializing in project management and design consulting, allowing them to capture a greater share of the estimated USD30-90 billion construction value chain by investing in expanding capabilities or strategic partnerships.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

viewpoints.title: AI adoption crucial for real estate services to build differentiating capabilities
viewpoints.description: McKinsey advises real estate services companies to strategically adopt AI, focusing on building proprietary workflows and data, governance models, institutional knowledge, and customer relationships, rather than developing underlying AI technologies. This approach allows them to differentiate their businesses and automate manual processes, like payment matching and billing in finance functions. Partnering for workflow redesign and employee training can accelerate AI transformation, leading to significant value creation and competitive advantage for service providers in the real estate sector.
viewpoints.source_title: ...the AI dilemma: to build, buy, or partner.

viewpoints.title: Policy support and regulatory reforms strengthening India's REIT market and services
viewpoints.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) introduced REIT (Amendment) Regulations in 2025 to enhance the regulatory framework, improve governance, transparency, and investor protection, and expand investment opportunities in India's REIT market. These reforms create a more structured and attractive environment for real estate investments, which in turn supports transaction advisors, property managers, and other service providers involved with REITs by fostering clearer operational guidelines and broader market participation.

viewpoints.title: Digital transformation enhancing transparency and efficiency in property transactions
viewpoints.description: The Indian government's ongoing digitisation of land records and digital property registration, alongside blockchain-based property management systems, is significantly improving transparency and easing property transactions. These initiatives, including geo-referencing over 360 million land parcels and integrating sub-registrar offices with revenue systems, reduce title disputes and accelerate project approvals. This digital transformation directly benefits property brokers, transaction advisors, and real estate data platforms by streamlining processes and boosting investor confidence.

viewpoints.title: Flexible workspaces driving significant demand for managed office solutions
viewpoints.description: Flexible workspace operators are emerging as a major force in India's commercial real estate market, becoming the second-largest occupier segment after technology in Q1 2026 office leasing. This reflects a strong and continued demand for managed and hybrid office spaces from corporates. This trend directly translates into increased opportunities for real estate services firms specializing in property management, brokerage, and advisory for co-working and flexible office solutions across major cities, particularly Bengaluru, Pune, Delhi-NCR, and Mumbai.

demand_drivers.description: The Indian real estate market's projected expansion from US$ 650 billion in 2025 to US$ 5.80 trillion by 2047 will naturally drive increased demand for real estate services across all segments, including residential, commercial, and industrial.

India's urban population is projected to reach 607.3 million by 2030, up from 522.4 million in 2025, fueling sustained demand for residential real estate, affordable housing, and urban infrastructure, which translates to higher demand for real estate services.

new_opportunities.description: Investment is increasingly focused on Tier II and III cities, supported by infrastructure development and rising occupier demand, presenting new geographical opportunities for real estate service providers to expand their brokerage, property management, and advisory services.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Expansion into Tier II and III cities

market_sizing.methodology: The broader Indian real estate market was valued at Rs. 54.96 lakh crore (US$ 650 billion) in 2025 and is projected to reach Rs. 553.38 lakh crore (US$ 5.80 trillion) by 2047. This growth in the underlying real estate market indicates a corresponding expansion in demand for real estate services, although specific market sizing for the services sub-industry is not provided.

demand_drivers.description: India's installed data center capacity is projected to reach 7.0–7.5 GW by 2030 and beyond, driven by AI and high-performance computing workloads. This necessitates substantial demand for related design, project management, and commissioning services for new data center facilities.

The shift to AI-native data centers, demanding higher structural load ratings, power densities, and advanced cooling solutions, requires a full-scale redesign of infrastructure. This transition drives specific demand for specialized design and consulting services within the data center real estate value chain.

new_opportunities.description: There is a growing opportunity for domestic players to localize manufacturing and deploy AI-native data center capabilities across the value chain. This presents a strategic opportunity for Indian engineering, project management, and design service providers to capture a greater market share.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Localisation of DC construction value chain

market_sizing.methodology: The cumulative construction-related opportunity for data centers in India is estimated at USD30 billion by FY30, scaling to USD90 billion by FY35. This includes services such as project management consulting and design consulting (within 'Design and construction') and specialized commissioning services, which are integral to the real estate services sector for specialized assets like data centers.
